Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, inherited rollout evidence, and both required wake-policy skill guides. Then I’ll inspect the two visual views before deciding on exactly one candidate and updating the required notes and reusable guidance.

The shelf consultation is mandatory here because this appears to be the common-seed architecture stage. Its rules require evidence-first transfer, so I’m now anchoring the candidate to the inherited scores, metrics, diagnostics, and optimizer notes before reading the mechanism references or proposing an edit.

All four sampled runs are direct-uniform still-water captures and share the same rendered trajectory; three use the same policy bytes, while one differs only in candidate source. I’m treating the shared capture as the strongest finite example and will use the inherited pre-capture divergence history as the failure baseline, rather than inventing differences among duplicate successful sheets.

The useful distinction is now clear: the isolated acceleration projection has already been evaluated and is behaviorally identical to the captured controller, whereas the extra joint-speed guard delayed capture. I’m consulting the shelf references now to transfer only the actuator-boundary invariant; this will not be used to retune gains or alter the successful gait.

The sampled A/B evidence is deterministic: after removing only the two issued-command columns, trajectory hashes match exactly; keyframes, capture time, score, and all applied motion match, while raw acceleration peaks fall from `74.20/85.64` to `31.416/31.416 rad/T²`. I’m recording that diagnosis and the falsifiable shelf transfer before touching the candidate, as required.

The pre-edit notes are complete. I’m now applying only the evidence-confirmed boundary projection: one parameter-owned acceleration limit and finite componentwise clamping of the two final commands. The successful feedback architecture and all active gait/steering parameters remain unchanged.

The candidate now honors the public acceleration envelope without changing the captured applied dynamics. I’m materially revising the stale near-miss lesson into the completed evidence chain—geometric completion gating produced capture, isolated projection preserved it exactly, and the speed guard was harmful—so later workers have a clear applicability boundary.

Both required provenance files are updated, so the candidate is structurally complete. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner now and will also run focused local schema/output checks.

The configured check-runner agent could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account. I’m preserving the same non-CFD validation scope by reading its configuration and executing the specified checks directly; this is an environment limitation, not a candidate failure.

The first prescribed check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: the same parent optimizer is marked “copied to guidance” twice in `README.md`, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. Both markers name the same optimizer. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, then rerunning the check; no task or evidence content changes.

All three prescribed checks now pass: guidance materiality, the Julia policy contract (including finite bounded outputs), and the editable-boundary check. I’m doing one final provenance review to confirm the candidate differs from the evaluated projected sample only in descriptive metadata and that no sibling candidate or out-of-scope solver edit was introduced.

Implemented exactly one candidate: an evidence-confirmed acceleration-projected completion-gated controller.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:66)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:37)

The candidate preserves the captured gait and steering while bounding issued accelerations at `1800 deg/T²`. Sampled evidence showed identical applied trajectories and capture behavior after projection.

Checks passed:

- Guidance materiality and notes
- Julia policy contract and bounded finite outputs
- Editable-file boundary

The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact prescribed commands were executed directly. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker in [README.md](README.md:123) that initially prevented the guidance checker from resolving the parent. No CFD was run.
